newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VETERAN MCCOIST INSPIRES RANGERS TO CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VETERAN MCCOIST INSPIRES RANGERS TO CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE WIN.

text.p: Ally McCoist, back in the side after being relegated to the substitutes' bench for last week's league match against Celtic, was the inspirational figure in Glasgow Rangers's first European Champions' League win for three and a half years on Wednesday.
The 34-year-old striker scored twice in the 2-1 group A win over Grasshopper Zurich.
McCoist scored a 66th minute penalty to break his four-year duck at this level and added his second six minutes later with an 18-metre strike.
The goals took McCoist's tally to 18 in European competition with Rangers.
That is joint top for a Scottish player with Willie Wallace who scored 18 for Celtic and Hearts.
"Thank goodness for that," said manager Walter Smith when he realised the goals were McCoist's first in the Champions' League.
"We are delighted to end the run of defeats. It would have been embarrassing to not win a game in the campaign."

Grasshopper, who must now beat Ajax Amsterdam at home in two weeks to be sure of progress to the last eight, were already 2-0 down when substitute Jan Berger volleyed their only goal in the 76th minute.
